Subject: Follow-up: FinTrust discovery - data handling & access controls

Hi Sam / Priya,

Great to meet earlier - thanks for the helpful call. Per our discussion I wanted to capture the key items and next steps on data handling and access controls so we have a clear path for your security review. TL;DR: Redwood supports PII minimization, configurable retention windows, detailed request logging, and role-based access with break-glass and auditable support access.

Summary of what we covered:
- PII: You indicated that account numbers and partial SSNs may appear in user prompts. Redwood can redact or mask PII at ingestion and supports token-level filtering in the routing layer.
- Data residency & retention: We can pin model inference in specific regions (US-EAST / EU-WEST) and configure per-customer retention policies (default: 30 days; configurable to 0 for ephemeral).
- Logging & audit: Full request/response metadata (timestamps, model id, user id hashes) are available for X days depending on plan; request bodies can be suppressed from logs on request.
- Access controls: RBAC with least-privilege roles, granular permissions for route management, and break-glass flow for emergency support access with automatic multi-person approval and audit trail.

Attachments: I attached a short SOC2 summary and a data retention mapping (spreadsheet) to illustrate defaults and options.

Next steps / asks from FinTrust:
1) Please confirm targeted retention window requirements (e.g., 0, 7, 30, 90 days).
2) Send any compliance questionnaire sections where you need specific artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption details).
3) If you want a proof-of-concept for RBAC + break-glass flows, we can schedule a 60 min session with Vivek (SE) next week.

I'll loop in Vivek and Rishi for technical detail on RBAC and support access flows.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Marissa - thanks for the summary. Couple of clarifying Qs from our side: 

1) For PII masking, can that be done at the edge (before hitting the model) or does it only happen in your control plane after ingestion? We have a principle of minimizing PII leaving our VPC.
2) Break-glass: what is the approval flow? We require 2-person approval and a detailed justification to be recorded. Is that supported out-of-the-box?
3) For retention = 0 (ephemeral), is there any portion of metadata retained (e.g., request ids, timestamps) for troubleshooting SLA incidents?

We also have a standard security questionnaire (I've attached the sections relevant to data handling) - would appreciate if Redwood can confirm who on your team will own responses.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: FinTrust discovery - data handling & access controls

Hi Sam - Vivek here from SE. Quick answers below and a recommended approach for the POC.

1) Edge masking: Yes, we support pre-ingest masking at the customer edge in Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) using our ingestion SDK and policies. For Hosted customers, we offer client-side SDK hooks (JS/Java) to perform regex/token-based redaction before sending requests to the API. We can provide sample code during the POC.

2) Break-glass approval: Supported. Our break-glass flow requires a 2-person approval for elevation to support-access mode. The system captures: who requested, who approved, time window, justification text, and a signed audit record. All events are immutable and routed to the customer audit log. The flow can be integrated with your SSO/SCIM for approver identities.

3) Retention=0: For strict ephemeral mode we do not persist raw request/response bodies. We do retain minimal operational metadata for a short troubleshooting window (request id, timestamp, routing node id) for up to 72 hours by default; that window can be shortened via contract to 0 if required. Those retained fields do not contain PII.

POC recommendation:
- 60-min session: architecture walkthrough (15m) + ingest/masking demo (25m) + RBAC/break-glass demo in a sandbox (20m).
- Pre-POC deliverables: we will share a sample config for RBAC roles and a redaction regex file.

I'll upload the RBAC config example and a short runbook after this email (attachments). Rishi will follow up with SOC2 artifacts and encryption details.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
